column1: # oracle-health allowlist — mutants that SURVIVE but are NOT oracle holes.
# Each row is an equivalent (behaviour cannot change) or dead (code not reached by
# the target) mutant. Listed here, oraclehealth reclassifies it as ALLOWLISTED and
# drops it from the kill-rate denominator, so a later run does not re-report it as a
# hole. A row must name the exact code that makes the mutation unobservable.
# Match key is (target, file, func, op, orig, new) with whitespace collapsed — NOT
# the line number, so an entry survives the construct moving to a new line and stops
# matching (fails safe, re-reporting) only when the construct itself changes.
# Columns (tab-separated): target  file  func  op  orig  new  class  reason
# class is "equivalent" or "dead". See README.md "The equivalent/dead allowlist".

column8: 6to4 reads the 4th octet from ip16[5]; no CIDR in privateNetworkCIDRs is longer than /16, so the 4th octet never affects IsPrivateOrLinkLocal's verdict — the oracle cannot observe this read shifting.
local-use NAT64 reads the 3rd octet from ip16[14]; no CIDR in privateNetworkCIDRs is longer than /16, so the 3rd octet never affects IsPrivateOrLinkLocal's verdict.

column5: if err != nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to decode nonce: %w", err) }
column8: nonce base64-decode guard; a bad nonce is still caught by the len(nonce)!=gcmNonceSize guard and, failing that, by the GCM tag in open(), so Decrypt still errors — invisible to a fails-on-tamper oracle.

column5: if len(nonce) != gcmNonceSize { return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid nonce length %d", len(nonce)) }
column8: nonce-length guard; open() feeds a wrong-length nonce to the GCM tag, which fails as an error (never a panic, per open()'s own doc comment), so dropping the length check is unobservable to a fails-on-tamper oracle.

column5: if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &encrypted); err != nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to deserialize encrypted data: %w", err) }
column8: DeserializeEncryptedData is never called by this tamper/round-trip target (it builds EncryptedData structs directly, never round-tripping through Serialize/Deserialize); covered by FuzzDeserializeEncryptedData.
